Prompt for Agent Team: Test PowerPoint Creation — Value Addition Pitch (Investor/Clients)
Project Context
This task relates to the AI Company Builder project at C:\Users\jmlus\light-speed-holdings. The system generates branded pitch decks from Markdown specs using python-pptx and LightSpeed brand tokens (navy #070A40, red #E63946, cyan #00BFFF, Arial type scale, 4px grid, official logo rules). A generation script lives at static/brand/templates/generate-pitch-deck.py and references ai_venture_studio_client_presentation.md (Part 5 of the client-facing docs).

Objective
Create a 13-slide PowerPoint presentation that pitches the value addition of our AI agent hierarchy platform to potential investors and clients. The deck must be fully brand-compliant, visually polished, and ready for stakeholder review or sales use.

Input / Reference Materials
Item	Path/Location	Purpose
Presentation spec	ai_venture_studio_client_presentation.md	Full narrative, slide-by-slide content guide (13 slides)
Brand tokens	brand/tokens/brand-tokens.json + brand/guidelines/brand-guidelines.md	Enforce navy/red/cyan palette, typography, logo usage, clear-space, no-AI-slop checklist
Company registry (KPIs/roles)	company-registry.yaml	Defines ATC >90%, velocity <60d, correction ratio, 3x capital efficiency — reference in slides as needed
Generation script (template)	static/brand/templates/generate-pitch-deck.py	Shows how Markdown → PPTX is built; adapt content into its input structure
Quality gate	ls-artifact-qa skill	Final visual/brand/QA check; must APPROVE before delivery
What to Produce
A .pptx file at static/brand/templates/value-add-pitch-investors-clients.pptx (or equivalent path) with exactly 13 slides following this structure:

Slide	Title / Focus	Key Content
1	Cover / Executive Summary	Company name, tagline, logo (brand-compliant), date
2	The Problem	Pain points for investors/clients in agent orchestration / AI company building
3	Our Solution	Platform overview (1‑sentence value prop)
4	Value Addition (CTO Portfolio D)	How agent hierarchies reduce cost/velocity/conflict — reference company-registry.yaml KPIs
5	Market Opportunity	TAM/SAM/SOM, AI/ML service provider landscape, SADC/Lighthouse pilot context
6	Business Model	Revenue streams, pricing, capital efficiency (3x target)
7	Traction / Lighthouse Pilots	Pilot results, outcomes, testimonials (if any)
8	Agent Registry & Orchestration	How the registry/YAML → Jinja2 → .opencode/agents/*.md pipeline works (high‑level)
9	Security & Trust	Zero‑trust, key rotation, RBAC, dashboard security (per governance docs)
10	Roadmap & Milestones	90‑day, 6‑month, 1‑year milestones
11	The Ask	Investment amount or client engagement terms
12	Team & Roles	Executive, Specialist, Department — per domain model
13	Closing / Next Steps	Contact, demo request, approval flow
Brand & Technical Requirements
✅ Palette: navy #070A40, red #E63946, cyan #00BFFF — used per brand guidelines Sec. 9
✅ Typography: Arial, type scale as defined in brand guidelines
✅ Logo: Official LightSpeed logo, placed per clear-space rules (do not resize, rotate, or recolor)
✅ No AI‑slop: No generic stock phrases, invented metrics, or fabricated claims. Every stat must map to a verified source (company-registry, ECL docs, pipeline models.yaml, etc.)
✅ Slide count: Exactly 13 (no more, no fewer)
✅ File format: .pptx generated via python-pptx (or the existing generate-pitch-deck.py adapted for this spec)
✅ Brand QA: Must pass ls-artifact-qa visual/brand checklist (run locally or via the skill; must output APPROVE)
Test / Verification Checklist (Agent Team)
Run the following and document results:

#	Test	Pass Criteria
1	uv run python static/brand/templates/generate-pitch-deck.py (or equivalent)	Deck generates without errors; 13 slides present
2	Brand token check	All slide backgrounds, text, and accents use only allowed hex codes; logo appears exactly once and per clear-space rules
3	Content fidelity	Every slide matches the spec in ai_venture_studio_client_presentation.md; no missing/extra sections
4	No fabricated claims	Cross‑check every statistic/organization name against company-registry.yaml, pipeline/models.yaml, docs/, or known-issues.md; flag any unverified content
5	ls-artifact-qa gate	Run the skill; result must be APPROVE. If FIX→RENDER, iterate on palette, typography, logo placement, or text conciseness
6	Exit‑code & build	Script exits 0; no ENOENT/path errors (recall the Vercel .vercelignore lesson — keep all generated assets inside static/brand/templates/ or explicitly allowed paths)
7	Accessibility basic check	Sufficient contrast (navy on cyan/red or reverse per brand grid), alt text on logo, no color‑only information
Deliverables
.pptx file at the agreed path, with 13 brand‑compliant slides
Short verification report (1‑2 paragraphs) covering:
Brand‑compliance status (APPROVE/FIX from ls-artifact-qa)
Any content flags (fabricated metrics, missing sources, etc.)
Exit code / build outcome
Optional: Modified/generate-pitch-deck.py snippet if the team adapted the script for this spec
Handoff Notes (for the agent team lead)
This deck replaces any previous investor/client pitch — it’s the single source of truth for value‑add messaging
All brand checks are non‑negotiable; the ls-artifact-qa gate is the final arbiter
If any KPI or stat from company-registry.yaml feels stale, flag it — the registry is the authoritative source, not the deck
Remember the /scripts/deploy/vercel-ignore-build.sh lesson: keep generated assets within static/brand/templates/ and avoid path shenanigans that trigger .vercelignore ENOENT failures
When in doubt, ask before inserting a metric or organization name that isn’t explicitly in the registry or a docs file
Prompt generated for the light‑speed holdings AI company builder project. Adapt paths/filenames as needed for your local environment, but keep the brand, KPI, and QA gates identical.

9: ## 1. Executive Summary
10: 
11: The AI Venture Studio is a **stage-gated, repeatable engine** that co-founds, validates, builds, and launches AI-native entities using shared technical infrastructure, agent stacks, data pipelines, and go-to-market engines. Since shipping Parts 1–5 in September 2026, the studio has delivered:

21: **Why it matters:** Each venture gets access to capital-efficient infrastructure, governance that scales without chaos, and a clear path from thesis to spin-out in under 60 days.

25: ## 2. The Studio Operating Engine
26: 
27: ```

44: **Three portfolio archetypes (Portfolios A–C)** — These represent the studio's core venture types: Enterprise Agent, B2B AI Workflow, and Sovereign Data. Each portfolio type integrates with the Model Mesh & Routing Engine (Section 4) through its designated model tier: Portfolio A with Frontier models, Portfolio B with Open-weights models, and Portfolio C with Local/Sovereign models.

46: **Four reservations (thesis-protecting framework)** — These are strategic guardrails that thesis-driven validation must satisfy before a venture progresses:

48: - Reservation 1: Constraint-first (Malawi constraints → global export)
49: - Reservation 2: AI-agnostic (works with any LLM provider)
50: - Reservation 3: PII-first (guardrails by default, not afterthought)
51: - Reservation 4: Capital-efficient (3–5× improvement over traditional routes)
52: 
53: **Note**: The "three" and "four" refer to distinct frameworks: Portfolio archetypes (A–C) vs. strategic reservations. Both are integral to the studio's stage-gated lifecycle and are referenced throughout this presentation.
54: 
55: **Portfolio D (Consumer Platforms)** — *Added per CTO validation*: High-volume, low-latency consumer-facing AI applications (e.g., personal assistants, education tutoring, retail recommendation systems) requiring sub-second execution, streaming UI, and edge/cost-optimized model cascading. This portfolio type complements the B2B‑focused A–C archetypes and aligns with the studio's target industries (Healthcare, Finance, Academia), which include both B2B and B2C use cases.

59: ## 3. Stage-Gated Development Lifecycle

62: |-------|----------|------------------|---------------|
63: | **1. Discovery** | Weeks 1–2 | Problem discovery & thesis definition across high-value operational bottlenecks | 3+ problem statements validated with internal stakeholders |

78: ### Model Mesh & Routing Engine

101: ### Engineering Directives
102: 
103: | Directive | Description |
104: |-----------|-------------|
105: | **Universal Protocol Proxy** | Single internal interface (LiteLLM or custom gateway) that decouples application code from underlying providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, local Ollama) |
106: | **Model Cascade & Dynamic Cost Router** | Simple extraction/classification → low-cost or open-weights models; multi-step reasoning or high-risk synthesis → top-tier frontier models only when task confidence drops below pre-set thresholds |
107: | **Deterministic Execution & State Tracking** | Graph/workflow orchestration logic decoupled from model inference using durable workers (Temporal, LangGraph); state persistence across API failures and connection interruptions |
108: | **Security & PII Guardrails** | Intermediary proxy layer that redacts/hashes PII before outgoing LLM requests; automated schema validation on all model outputs before database commits |

112: ## 5. Core Performance Metrics (Part 5)
113: 
114: | Metric | Goal | Why It Matters | CFO KPI Mapping |
115: |--------|------|----------------|-----------------|
116: | **Agentic Task Completion (ATC) Rate** | >90% end-to-end execution without manual intervention | Measures autonomous agent efficacy; directly impacts capital efficiency | Maps to **Cost per Agent** and **ROI per Department** — higher ATC reduces per-agent operational cost |
117: | **Velocity to MVP** | <60 days from Phase 1 thesis approval to Phase 3 customer deployment | Speed-to-market; competitive advantage; reduces burn | Maps to **Budget Utilization** — faster velocity reduces burn rate and preserves runway |
118: | **Manual Correction Ratio** | Track human override count per 1,000 executed agent actions | Quality signal; identifies where guardrails or model routing need adjustment | Maps to **Revenue per Task** — lower correction ratios indicate higher task quality and revenue efficiency |
119: | **Capital Efficiency per Spin-Out** | 3–5× capital efficiency compared to traditional seed rounds | Shared infrastructure, agent stacks, and data pipelines dramatically reduce per-venture cost | Maps to **Cost per Agent** and **Budget Utilization** — shared services reduce marginal costs per venture |
120: 
121: **Studio-level vs. company-level KPIs**: The four core metrics above are *studio-level* performance indicators measuring venture-creation effectiveness. The CFO's registry KPIs (Budget Utilization, Cost per Agent, ROI per Department, Total Revenue, Revenue Margin, Revenue per Task) are *company-level* financial metrics tracking Lightspeed Holdings' overall health. Both frameworks are complementary and should be reported separately — studio KPIs demonstrate venture success, while company KPIs ensure organizational financial discipline.
122: 
123: **3–5× capital efficiency derivation**: The 3–5× figure is derived from comparative analysis of traditional seed-round cost structures (legal, recruiting, infrastructure setup per venture) vs. studio shared-infrastructure economics (model mesh, agent stacks, data pipelines amortized across portfolios). A detailed annex with baseline assumptions is available on request.
124: 
125: **Velocity to MVP scope clarification**: The <60-day goal measures the subset from **Phase 2 validation approval** (positive buyer commitments, technical feasibility confirmed) to **Phase 3 minimal MVP deployment** with a design partner, not the full end-to-end lifecycle from Phase 1 thesis to spin-out (which follows the 4-phase lifecycle: ~22 weeks total). 147:

150: 2. **Finance** — Real-time fraud detection, automated risk assessment, compliance monitoring
